in_hebrew.name: לזאר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם לזאר מקורו במילה העברית 'עזר', שפירושה עזרה או סיוע. הוא קשור קשר הדוק למילה 'אלוהים', שפירושה אלוהים. לכן, ניתן לפרש את השם לזאר כ'אלוהים עזר' או 'אלוהים הוא עזר'. השם מופיע בברית הישנה וקשור לדמותו של לזרוס, אחיו של מרתה ומרי, שעליו דיבר ישו בברית החדשה.

in_greek.name: Λάζαρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λάζαρος προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'עזר' (ezer), που σημαίνει 'βοήθεια' ή 'συνδρομή'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Λάζαρος είναι ο αδελφός της Μάρθας και της Μαρίας, τον οποίο ανέστησε ο Ιησούς από τους νεκρούς. Το όνομα έχει ισχυρή πνευματική σημασία και συμβολίζει την παρέμβαση και τη δύναμη του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Lazare
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lazare derivatur ex voce hebraea 'ezer', quae significat 'auxilium' seu 'adiutorium'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Lazare erat celebre propter miraculum resurrectionis Lazari, amici Jesu, narratum in Novo Testamento. Nomen hoc habet magnam significationem spiritualem et indicat potentiam et interventum Dei.

in_english.name: Lazare

It carries a rich history in Christian tradition and is often linked with themes of resurrection and salvation.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Lazare" is derived from the Latin word "Lazarus," which means "helped by God." Throughout history, the name Lazare has been associated with a powerful resurrection narrative from the New Testament. The most well-known Lazarus story is of a man named Lazarus of Bethany, who was born blind and died. Jesus, upon hearing of his friend's death, travelled to Bethany to resurrect him, ultimately bringing the man back to life. This inspiring and miraculous tale gave rise to several variations and interpretations of the name Lazare in various cultures around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Lazare" can be derived from both its etymology and the historical events tied to it. In its simplest form, the name symbolizes hope in divine intervention and an affirmation of faith in a God who helps, protects, and raises up those who are in need.

biblical_reference.note: The raising of Lazarus is a significant miracle attributed to Jesus in the Gospel of John.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Lazarus of Bethany, a friend of Jesus, was raised from the dead by him. The name Lazare carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
